newsitem.title: UK: LPG prices down in Europe but steady in East.
newsitem.headline: LPG prices down in Europe but steady in East.

text.p: Liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) prices slipped in Europe this week on the back of a fall in U.S. prices, but levels in the Middle East Gulf and East Asia remained steady, dealers said.
"Prices have been weaker in the U.S.," said a trader. "But after all, they're not so weak now. And stocks in the U.S. are still pretty low, so there's no reason for any sharp decrease."

He added that all oil products including LPG have been closely following gas oil, whose fall worldwide on Thursday prompted a drop on crude and other products, but this did not represent a fundamental lack of demand.
In Europe, prices were up at the beginning of the week. An 8,500-tonne propane cargo was traded mid-week at $272 a tonne cif Germany, but a trader said the price would not be repeatable now.
"Propane is back in the $260s now, perhaps even the low $260s", he said. "The next trade will have a six in it."

Butane was also firm early in the week, with a 10,000-tonne cargo sold at $240 a tonne cif U.K. east coast. The seller of this cargo said butane had been supported by naphtha, an alternative feedstock for petrochemical cracking.
